#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.644 (18.3.1.73 row) a: "Office requires that the r attribute be between 1 and 1048576 inclusive, and shall be in non-decreasing order". No note on a row without r: nothing Microsoft documents decides POS-1, so it rests on the consensus, and Excel is asked (request 4).
#     status: decided; Excel confirms it (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly": every r-less layout reads positionally, and every decided row agrees)

If this attribute is not specified and the cell is the first c element in the parent row collection, the cell shall be located in the first column." Agrees; it is Office's own documentation, so the basis is excel:doc.
#     status: decided; Excel confirms it (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly")
#   POS-3: A cell whose r names another row than its <row>'s: nothing decides where it is.
#     source: none in ECMA-376 for worksheets

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 has a note for the EXTERNAL-link cell (2.1.838, 18.14.1 cell) c: "Office requires that cell reference be within the row of the parent row element", and none for the worksheet c element. Not applied; it suggests Excel treats the mismatch as damage.

#   POS-5: Explicit positions that go backwards: a row r below the previous row's, or a cell r left of the previous cell's in its row (equal is POS-4). A row r EQUAL to the previous row's continues that row (round 3, X2): its cells are row n's, and must still ascend after the earlier ones (otherwise POS-4 or POS-5 applies). An r-less cell in such a row is undecided:repeated-row-rless (nothing observed says whether it continues the column count or starts at column A, as 2.1.590 c says of a first <c>).
#     source: none for backwards; for an equal row, Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly": two <row r="2"> elements are MERGED, B2 = 3 read beside A2 = 2; gate round 3 X2)
#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.644 a requires rows in NON-DECREASING order: a row r EQUAL to the previous row's meets Office's requirement, and Excel merges it (above).

#   VAL-1: A string's value is the <t> directly under <si>/<is>, or under <r>, concatenated; <rPh> and <phoneticPr> are not part of it.

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.673 (18.4.6 rPh) a and 2.1.671 (18.4.3 phoneticPr) b: "Excel restricts phonetic text to the Japanese language"; 2.1.675 (si) and 2.1.630 (is): at most 32767 r and rPh children. Nothing contradicts.
#     status: decided; Excel confirms it (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly": phonetic runs left out)

#   VAL-2: t="d" holds an ISO 8601 date, the serial of that moment in the workbook's system. Decided: YYYY-MM-DD, and YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm, :ss and .fff (no zone, at most 3 fraction digits), from the system's first non-Lotus date (1900-03-01; 1904-01-01) to 9999-12-31. Everything else unreadable.

#     source: ECMA-376 Part 1 18.18.11 (ST_CellType d: "Cell contains a date in the ISO 8601 format") and 18.17.4 (the ISO 8601 lexical forms: complete extended calendar date, time of day, and the two joined by T; fractional seconds "should" have at most three digits; hour 24 is not allowed)

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.660 (18.3.1.96 v) d: "Office supports only a limited number of date formats possible using ISO 8601, as listed in the Notes field" - and no list follows, so Microsoft does not document which forms Excel reads; the decided forms rest on ECMA alone and are asked of Excel (request 4). 18.17.4 also allows a time-of-day alone (08:30), which the spec leaves undecided: kept undecided, reported.

#     status: decided forms decided; the rest unreadable (IsoDate). Excel REPAIRS every t="d" workbook (request 4, SETTLED.md "Repaired"): the decided forms agree with it (excel:observed); the undecided ones stay refused, although Excel shows values for some (gate round 3 X13, by X1)

#   VAL-3: workbookPr/@date1904 1 or true: serial 0 is 1904-01-01 and there is no 1900-02-29; 0, false or absent: the 1900 system. It governs display, --period, ISO criteria, t="d" decoding, typed date writes (1904 serial = 1900 serial - 1462; a date before 1904-01-01 refused) and every echo. A STRICT workbook (conformance="strict") draws dates like the compatibility system: 0 is 1900-01-00 and 60 is 1900-02-29 (round 3, X10).
#     source: ECMA-376 Part 1 18.2.28 and 18.17.4.1 (the 1904 system's base date is 1904-01-01, serial 0); Microsoft, "Date systems in Excel"

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.585 (18.2.28 workbookPr) j (Office 2013 and later): "If workbook@conformance equals 'strict', the 1900 date system is used. Otherwise the 1900 compatibility date system is used. Excel does not support negative serial numbers." It says a STRICT book uses the true 1900 system (ECMA 18.17.4.1: base 1899-12-30, no 1900-02-29). EXCEL OBSERVED CONTRADICTS IT (request 4, SETTLED.md "A strict workbook": TEXT, DAY, MONTH and YEAR over 0, 1, 2, 59, 60 and 61 in a strict book give 1900-01-00 to 1900-02-29 and 1900-03-01, the compatibility system), and Excel observed wins (decision 40; gate round 3 X10).
#     status: decided; a negative serial's display in a 1904 book undecided (Excel's TEXT draws -1904-01-01 there, SETTLED.md "1904")

#   VAL-4: A part is UTF-8 (with or without a BOM) or UTF-16 (BOM, LE or BE). A part DECLARING windows-1252 or ISO-8859-1, or a UTF-16LE part with no BOM declaring UTF-16 (XML 1.0 Appendix F), is read in that encoding (round 3, X5) - within what Excel was shown (round 4): a windows-1252 part holding a non-ASCII byte other than E9 (80 to 9F included, where windows-1252 and ISO-8859-1 differ), an ISO-8859-1 part holding any non-ASCII byte, and a UTF-16BE part with no BOM are undecided, so refused naming the part. Any other declared encoding is undecided, so refused naming the part. Bytes invalid in the part's encoding (invalid UTF-8) are damage, refused naming the part.

#     source: XML 1.0 4.3.3 (every processor reads UTF-8 and UTF-16) and Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly": a sharedStrings part declared windows-1252 holding the byte E9 reads Café; a worksheet declared ISO-8859-1, holding ASCII bytes only, reads; a sharedStrings part in UTF-16LE declared UTF-16 with no BOM reads from the declaration; gate round 3 X5; round 4 refuses the bytes and byte order Excel was not shown, which round 3 had decided from the spec's wording alone). The spec cited ECMA-376 Part 2 6.2.5 a ("XML content shall be encoded using either UTF-8 or UTF-16"), but that clause covers the parts Part 2 itself defines, not SpreadsheetML parts
#     MS-OI29500: none (MS-OI29500's Part 2 notes, 2.1.1749 to 2.1.1752, say nothing of encodings)
#     status: UTF-8, UTF-16, and declared windows-1252 (ASCII and E9), ISO-8859-1 (ASCII) and BOM-less UTF-16LE decoded; anything else refused
#   VAL-5: A part that ends before its root element closes, or has any other well-formedness error, is damaged.
#     status: refused, naming the part; Excel repairs a cut-off sheet, sharedStrings, styles or rels part and REFUSES to open a cut-off workbook part (request 4, SETTLED.md "Repaired")

#   VAL-6: A number is xsd:double, whitespace collapsed (<v> 42 </v>, 1E3, .5, 5. and -0 are numbers). A leading +, NaN, INF, -INF and a lexical value past the largest double (1e400) are DAMAGE, so unreadable (round 3, X6: Excel repairs them into text or #NULL!; B4 read +5 as 5 and INF and NaN as non-finite numbers); inf, nan and a comma decimal are unreadable; an empty <v> is "" only on a text-typed cell (decision 37).
#     source: B4 round 2 (B4R1-EVAL-2/3/4), as amended by Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "Repaired": val-b4-numbers; gate round 3 X6)

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.660 (18.3.1.96 v) b: a number "shall be a textual representation of a double-precision floating point number"; "If the cell contains a Boolean, the value shall be 1 to specify true and 0 to specify false"; an error is one of #NULL!, #DIV/0!, #VALUE!, #REF!, #NAME?, #NUM!, #N/A. THE BOOLEAN NOTE CONTRADICTS the spec's "a boolean is 1, 0, true or false": by the spec's own rule the note wins, so `true` and `false` in a t="b" cell are undecided:bool-word here (refused). Excel REPAIRS them (request 4: TRUE and FALSE shown for the words, text for TRUE and 2), so they stay refused (gate round 3 X15, by X1).
#     status: decided; booleans 1 and 0 only (the note); +5, NaN, INF, -INF and 1e400 unreadable

#   VAL-7: A <t> WITHOUT xml:space="preserve" loses its leading and trailing XML whitespace (space, tab, LF, CR), in shared strings and inline strings; internal whitespace (a tab included) is kept, and so is a space XML does not count as whitespace (NBSP). Trimming is per <t> element (the attribute is per element), before _xHHHH_ escapes are decoded (an escaped space is no XML whitespace). t="str" <v> text is NOT trimmed (no evidence; decision 37). A rich-text run's <t> (under <r>) with whitespace at an end and no preserve is undecided:run-end-whitespace (round 4: Excel was shown <t> directly under <si> and <is> only), so its string is unreadable.

#     source: Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly", ask-space: ' lead' reads lead (LEN 4), a line feed, two spaces, x and a line feed read x, three spaces read an empty string, in shared and inline strings alike; gate round 3 X4). The internal half and NBSP rest on Excel's own writing (decision 40's second source): Excel-saved corpus files hold <t> elements with no xml:space and internal runs of spaces (542 elements in 123 files carrying Excel 2016's revision namespace; 383,696 in 12,623 more files naming Microsoft Excel), internal line feeds (512 in 47), and NBSP at their ends (40 in 12), which Excel reads back from its own files. The internal TAB (round 4, golden item 6): no corpus file Excel 2016 or later saved (Application Microsoft Excel or Microsoft Macintosh Excel with the xr namespace: 1,940 files) holds a tab in any <t>, with or without xml:space; older Excel files hold 200 such <t> with no xml:space (83 in 24 files naming Microsoft Excel, 19 of them AppVersion 12.0000 or 14.0300; 117 in 2 naming Microsoft Macintosh Excel); and Excel for Mac 16.113.4 itself, saving val-xescape for request 4, wrote <t>a<TAB>b</t> with no xml:space (the shared string _x0009_ decoded to), which SETTLED.md reads as a tab (X3): excel:written
#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.678 a (as Gate D cites it; not re-read this round): Excel applies the W3C space rules from xml:space; it says nothing of text without one. Excel trims it (above).
#     status: decided; a run's <t> with end whitespace and no preserve undecided (round 4: refused, listed in UNSETTLED)
#   XSTR: Text escapes _xHHHH_ decode to the character, _x0009_ and _x000A_ included (round 3, X3); _x005F_ escapes a lead underscore; CDATA is text.
#     source: ECMA-376 Part 1 22.9.2.19 (ST_Xstring); Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly": _x0009_ and _x000A_ in element text decode to a tab and a line feed; gate round 3 X3)

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.1747 (22.9.2.19 ST_Xstring) a: "Office does not allow the newline (0x000A) or tab (0x0009) characters to be escaped in this simple type's contents"; b: CR shall be escaped; c: _x005f_ only to escape the lead underscore of an _xHHHH_ form. That note says what Office WRITES; Excel READS an escaped tab or line feed as the character (above).

#   PKG-1: Parts are found through relationships: the workbook through _rels/.rels's officeDocument, sharedStrings and styles through the workbook's rels by TYPE, transitional and strict. A Target resolves against its source part's folder, or from the root with a leading /. Part names match ASCII case-insensitively.
#     source: ECMA-376 Part 2 6.2.2.3 (part name equivalence is ASCII case-insensitive), 6.5 and Annex A (relationships, relative references)

#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.1749 (Part 2 6.2.2.2): "Office will not load a package containing parts with non-ASCII characters in their names" (every name here is ASCII); and, among the Part 2 notes (2.1.1749 to 2.1.1752), that Office uses STORE as well as DEFLATE. Nothing contradicts.
#     status: decided; Excel confirms it (request 4, SETTLED.md "Read cleanly": other names, absolute and .. Targets, strict types, a relocated workbook part)

#   PKG-2: No relationship: the part is ABSENT (no string table; every cell General). A relationship to a STYLES part that is missing: absent too, no styles, every cell General (round 4). A relationship to a sharedStrings or worksheet part that is missing, or a part that fails its CRC or inflate, or passes the cap: a DAMAGED package.

#     source: ECMA-376 Part 2; Excel observed (request 4: pkg-missing-styles, a relationship to a missing styles part, opened with no repair and saved A1 = 1, its one cell, as a number; gate round 4, golden item 1)

#     status: absent decided; damaged refused, naming the part. Excel REPAIRS a sharedStrings part with no relationship (Removed Records) and a styles part with no relationship (Repaired Records: General), and a relationship to a missing sharedStrings or sheet part (X1: damage); it opened a relationship to a missing STYLES part cleanly (pkg-missing-styles: absent)
#   PKG-3: A t="s" value that is not a non-negative integer below the table's length (no table included) is unreadable.
#     MS-OI29500: MS-OI29500 2.1.660 b: "the value shall be a zero-based index into the shared string table". Agrees.
#     status: unreadable, named; Excel REPAIRS every such cell (request 4, SETTLED.md "Repaired": Removed Records), so they stay refused (X1)
#   PKG-4: Every part the read path reads whole has the write path's caps; a part past one is refused.
#     source: decision 33; surgical.rs PART_DECOMPRESS_CAP (512 MiB) and TOTAL_DECOMPRESS_CAP (2 GiB)
#   PKG-5: A command on ONE sheet reads no other sheet's part; the package is opened once; a command over every sheet reads each part a bounded number of times.
#     status: resource checks with a wide bound

#   NUM-1: A figure from finite cells that is not itself a finite double (a sum or mean past 1.8e308; a stddev or variance whose intermediate overflows) has no value: NOT A REAL ANSWER, naming it. An AVERAGE over a sum that overflows is #NUM! too, so refused (round 3, X7).

#     source: Excel specifications and limits (largest number 9.99999999999999E+307); KB "Floating-point arithmetic": overflow is #NUM!; Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "Overflow": SUM, AVERAGE, STDEV and VAR over 9E+307, 9E+307, 1 give #NUM!; STDEV and VAR over 1E+200, -1E+200, 0 give #NUM! while SUM and AVERAGE give 0; gate round 3 X7)

#   PER-1: --period buckets a serial by its date ROUNDED TO THE NEAREST SECOND (round 3, X8; it was the millisecond). Past 9999-12-31 after rounding, below the system's first day (1900-01-01; 1904-01-01), or negative is not a date (rows_not_a_date). In the 1904 system serial 0 is 1904-01-01. The 1900 system's serial 60 (Excel's fictional 1900-02-29) stays undecided:1900-02-29. Its serial 0, Excel's fictional 1900-01-00, is no date by B1's floor (--period names no date below serial 61), not by Excel, whose DAY, MONTH and YEAR give 1900-01-00 (round 4: b1:floor).

#     source: Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "--period": DAY, MONTH and YEAR round the serial to the nearest second - 0.7 ms before midnight is the next day; 8.6 ms before the end of 9999-12-31 is #NUM!; a negative serial is #NUM! in a 1904 book; gate round 3 X8). Each PER-1 row whose serial Excel was asked about is checked against its DAY, MONTH and YEAR in the ask-per1 workbooks here (per1_answer; excel:asked)

#   REPAIR: A shape Excel REPAIRS is damage (round 3, X1). In a repaired file a cell whose saved value equals the rule's stays decided (excel:observed); a cell where it differs, and every undecided cell, is refused (excel:repaired). A byte-identical repeated cell stays one cell (Excel removes the extra record and keeps the value). A file Excel refuses to open is refused (excel:refused). The undecided t="d" forms (X13), error codes outside the documented eight (X14) and the boolean words (X15) stay refused by this rule.
#     source: Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "How a repair counts"; gate round 3 X1, X13 to X15)
#   VOLATILE: A volatile formula's value (NOW, TODAY, RAND, RANDBETWEEN, RANDARRAY, OFFSET, INDIRECT, INFO, CELL) is never compared with Excel's: Excel recalculates it (round 3, X12).
#     source: Excel observed (request 4, SETTLED.md "One spurious contradiction": pos-rless-formulas C1, a NOW())
# RESOURCE BOUNDS (T rows): one-sheet commands 1.0 s; workbook-summary 6.0 s at 1,000 sheets and 12.0 s at 2,000. Wall time, measured
#   on the development machine with its other services running (load 10 to 17): master took 3.07 s for
#   one sheet of 1,000 and 0.55 ms a sheet for workbook-summary over 10, growing with the count; Python's
#   zipfile and expat read every part of 2,000 sheets in 0.14 s. They guard the complexity (one open, no
#   other sheet read, each part read a bounded number of times), not the speed. See ONE_SHEET_BOUND.
# FORMAT. Tab-separated; a line starting # is a comment. Text fields escape \ \t \n \r and other control
#   X  <shape> <file | runtime:<kind>:<n>> <date system 1900|1904> <what the shape is>
#        expect: n:<number> | s:<text> | b:TRUE|FALSE | e:<code> | blank | date:<iso>@<serial> |
#                nonfinite:<spelling> | unreadable:<kind> (the value is undecided: never a value, blank or "")
#                | refuse:<aspect> (the cell's PLACE is undecided: no value, and no write into it)
#        shown:  the grid's text for the cell (get-range, view-sheet), or - where it is not judged
#                (a text's grid text is the text itself)
#        raw:    the value's spelling in the file, which the grid may show (backticked) for a value it
#                cannot read; - for a decided value
#        A date's serial is compared within 1e-8 days: which double a moment with a time is, is not decided.
#        used <A1:B2> (sheet-summary's range), nonblank <n> (sheet-summary), uncached <n> and volatile <n>
#        (clear-recalculation-flag's audit, without --clear), view content|empty (view-sheet), clear kept
#        (clear-recalculation-flag --clear on a copy leaves fullCalcOnLoad set, read by the test's own parser)
#        refuse: every command that prints a figure, a value or a count, and every write, exits non-zero with
#        an error naming the part; none prints a value. list-sheets is reported, not judged.
#   W  <shape> <sheet> <cell> <input> <checks> <basis> <must> <rule>                a write (set-cell, on a copy)
#        checks, ;-joined: exit=0 | refuse | v:<cell>=n:<x>|none (the cached <v> the write left, read by the
#        TEST's own parser of the output part) | flag=0|1 (fullCalcOnLoad after the write) | deps=<cells> (named
#        by the report) | echo=<field>:<value> (the report's field). Every write also checks, by that parser,
#        that the written cell is where it was asked to be and every other cell kept its place and value.
#        command: the CLI arguments after <path> <sheet>, |-joined. checks, ;-joined <field>=<expect>:
#        value|mean|std_dev|total_matched|rows_not_a_date = n:<x> | refuse (exit non-zero, or NOT A REAL
#        ANSWER in the output); rows=<r,r>; distinct=<v>:<n>,...; groups=<key>:n:<x>|refuse,... (a group's
#        refuse: its figure null and the group named beside the overflow, group-by's own convention). A bucket
#        missing because its row was counted in rows_not_a_date is a refusal, not a wrong answer.
